Empires & Puzzles Tinsel Review: The Gnome Tinkerer

Is Tinsel just a festive decoration or a lethal weapon? We break down this fast-mana Ice hero, exploring her unique tile-scaling debuffs and why a specific 2024 mechanic change has given this 2022 hero a sudden resurgence in the top-tier meta. Don't let her small stature fool you.
Tinsel: Blue Tiles, Blinding Lights, and Toy Destruction
Tinsel: The Gnome Tinkerer Who Turns Blue Tiles into Nightmares

Tinsel is a 5-star Ice (Blue) hero from the Winter Family (Santa's Challenge), originally released in December 2022. She arrives as a Fast mana "Hit-3" Wizard who thrives on board manipulation. Unlike the brute force of some seasonal heroes, Tinsel is a technician; her power fluctuates wildly based on the number of Ice shields currently on the board. While she lacks a costume, her unique mechanics have kept her surprisingly relevant in specific offensive niches long after her stats have started to gather dust.

Tinsel's design is a delightful blend of steampunk and fantasy workshop aesthetics. She sports oversized goggles, a heavy apron, and wields a massive, contraption-like hammer that looks like it could build a toy train or demolish a tank with equal efficiency. The art captures her "Tinkerer" persona perfectly—she looks busy, determined, and slightly dangerous. It is a refreshing change from the high-fantasy knights and dragons, leaning into the whimsical yet mechanical side of the Winter event.

When looking at Tinsel's stats in the context of the current meta (2025-2026), the reality is stark. With a base power of around 851, she is significantly behind the curve of modern heroes who regularly push past 1300 power. Her defense (807) and health (1444) are particularly low by today's standards, making her a "glass cannon." Without Limit Break 2 (Alpha Aethers) and full emblems, she will struggle to survive a single hit from modern snipers. She relies entirely on her Fast speed to impact the game before she is removed from the board.

"Malevolent Toys" is a skill that rewards playing the board. At Fast speed, dealing 340% damage to three targets is a solid baseline—it's enough to soften up a defense or finish off weakened foes. However, the real magic lies in the variable debuffs.
The Defense Down starts at a modest -14% but can scale up to a crushing -54% if you have 8 Ice shields on the board. Similarly, the Accuracy Down scales from -10% to -50%.
This makes Tinsel a "high ceiling, low floor" hero. On a bad board, she is a weak hitter with negligible debuffs. On a blue-heavy board, she is devastating.
She summons Elf Minions for all allies. These are fairly weak (10% HP/Attack), serving mostly as a small meat shield or a way to override negative minion effects, rather than a primary win condition.
Let's break down the math behind the Tinkerer.
Fast. She charges in 8 tiles. With a level 29 Magic/Styx troop or level 23 Mana troop (plus her Wizard talent node), she can easily reach the 7-tile break point, making her extremely snappy.

340% damage to 3 targets. With her base attack of 852 (un-emblemed/un-LB), that's roughly 2900 damage output distributed. Modern heroes hit harder, but at Fast speed, this is still respectable chip damage.

Tinsel does not possess any modern passive skills. This is a significant disadvantage compared to newer heroes who often come with built-in cleanses, mana boosts, or damage reduction.

At the start of the battle, her attack is increased by 20% for 6 turns. This fits her perfectly. As a Fast hero, you want to fire her early. The attack boost helps her initial hit pierce through modern defense stats despite her older base power.

Layering Tinsel's blind with another blinder can render the enemy team completely ineffective, causing them to miss virtually all attacks while you pick them apart.
Ogima, Grimble, and Topaz love seeing Tinsel. She gives them free food (minions) to destroy and gain mana or deal damage.

If you are lucky enough to pull Tinsel early, she is a fantastic asset. She will likely be your primary blue damage dealer for a long time. Focus on getting her to 3/70 and see if she survives; if she does, she is worth the scopes. Her ability to blind enemies will help you punch up against stronger teams in raids.
